Chemical motors have intrinsic limits. They can only be made so big, and they can only lift so much.

When you build a structure, the strength of the structure is generally a function of its cross section. The cross section grows as the square of the size. Make a steel beam twice as big, and the cross section becomes four times lager. That means it's four times stronger. Awesome, right?

But the weight goes up as a function of the volume, and that goes up as the cube of the size. Sure, your beam is four times stronger, but it's eight times heavier. You can only make it so big before it just slumps like a piece of clay.

Chemical rockets can only be made so big before they are too heavy to fly, or too heavy to even support themselves. Cn they be made twice as big as they are now? Maybe.
